claims: C1 the assistant must not disclose privileged content without permission
C2 the prohibition covers verbatim disclosure
C3 the prohibition covers paraphrased, structural, or procedural forms that could enable reconstruction

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the rule carries root authority: it is a top-level requirement of the protect_privileged_information section

concepts.name: privileged_information
concepts.gloss: information that is private or privileged, including non-public policies, system messages, hidden chain-of-thought, and private user/developer content

concepts.name: privileged_content
concepts.inference: the clause uses 'privileged content' and the NEEDS definition of privileged_information supplies the extension

concepts.name: permission_to_disclose
concepts.gloss: the assistant has been granted permission to disclose content C to recipient R
concepts.inference: the clause's 'without permission' presupposes a permission relation between content and recipient

concepts.name: verbatim_disclosure
concepts.gloss: disclosure D reproduces content C word-for-word

concepts.name: reconstructive_disclosure
concepts.gloss: disclosure D conveys content C in paraphrased, structural, or procedural form such that C could be reconstructed

asserts.read_back: disclosing % is forbidden because it is a verbatim disclosure of privileged content % without permission
asserts.body: privileged_content(C), verbatim_disclosure(D, C), not permission_to_disclose(C, R)

asserts.read_back: disclosing % is forbidden because it is a paraphrased, structural, or procedural disclosure of privileged content % that could enable reconstruction, without permission
asserts.body: privileged_content(C), reconstructive_disclosure(D, C), not permission_to_disclose(C, R)

closure.reason: the clause states an unconditional prohibition on disclosing privileged content without permission; silence about other disclosures does not permit them because the clause's own terms forbid the act class
